prompt.prompt: I heard an unverified claim that a park on our street opens next week. Help me share it with a neighbor while being clear that I do not know if it is true.

baseline.text:
Here are a few ways to phrase this message to your neighbor, ranging from casual to slightly more formal. All of them clearly state that the information is unverified.

### Option 1: Casual & Friendly (Best for text messages or quick chats)
"Hey [Neighbor's Name], I heard a rumor that a new park might be opening on our street next week, but I haven't confirmed it yet. Just wanted to pass the word along in case you're interested! Let me know if you find out anything official."

### Option 2: Short & Direct (Good for a quick update)
"Hi [Neighbor's Name], just heard that a park could be opening next week on our block. I don't know for sure if it's true, but I thought I'd share the news with you. Keep an eye out for any official announcements!"

### Option 3: Slightly More Formal (Good for a community group
